title: The borrowed umbrella
text:
It had been raining since breakfast, and by the time the bell rang for home, the school yard looked like a shallow brown lake. Dewi stood at the gate with her bag held over her head. She had forgotten her umbrella again.

"Here, take mine," said a gruff voice. It was Pak Hadi, the caretaker, holding out a huge black umbrella with a bent handle. Dewi had always thought he was a grumpy man, because he never smiled when children ran in the corridor.

"But then you will get wet," she said.

"I have a raincoat," he replied, and patted his pocket. "Bring it back tomorrow."

Dewi walked home under the big umbrella. Halfway there, she noticed a small boy from Year 1 sitting in a bus shelter, hugging his knees. He was not wearing a coat. His lips were pressed together as if he was trying not to cry. Dewi crossed the road and held the umbrella over him.

"Is your mum coming?" she asked.

"She said she would be late," he whispered. "Because of the rain."

So Dewi waited with him. They counted the cars that splashed past, and she taught him a clapping game. Twenty minutes later a woman in a green scarf hurried round the corner, out of breath, and swept the boy into her arms.

The next morning Dewi found Pak Hadi sweeping leaves near the gate. She gave the umbrella back and told him what had happened. For a moment he said nothing. Then the corners of his mouth lifted, just a little.

"A good umbrella," he said, "is one that keeps more than one person dry."

From that day on, Dewi noticed that Pak Hadi did smile. He just did it very quietly.
